# findOrCreatePerson — POST /people/findOrCreate

Find a person, or create one if nothing matches

## Verified behaviors

- **An empty body creates a blank person record** — Every field is optional, including the name, so `{}` is a valid payload on both create endpoints: create answers 201 Stored, and findOrCreate — with no criteria to match on — answers 201 UnmatchedStored. Each call leaves a nameless person record behind. ([replay](../behaviors/empty-bodies-create-blank-people.md))
- **Below the match threshold, findOrCreate quietly creates a duplicate** — A name alone never reaches the minimum match combination, so no match is attempted: the payload is stored as a brand-new person record even though the person is already in the database. There is no 'unmatched' to inspect — the no-match case is the create case. ([replay](../behaviors/findorcreate-below-threshold-creates-a-duplicate.md))
- **findOrCreate drops a vanId that matches nothing** — Where create echoes a plausible unknown vanId back as a phantom match, findOrCreate just drops it: the ordinary match runs on the rest of the payload — here finding the existing person by name and email — and would have created a person had it found nothing. The vanId only matters when it names a real person. ([replay](../behaviors/findorcreate-ignores-an-unknown-vanid.md))
- **Above the match threshold, findOrCreate returns the existing person** — Name plus email clears the minimum match combination, so the existing person comes back as a 302 match stub with a Location header, and nothing is written. ([replay](../behaviors/findorcreate-returns-the-existing-match.md))

## Behavior

Runs the same match as POST /people/find and, when nothing matches, stores the payload as a new person record.

Outcomes:

- **The body supplies a `vanId` that exists** — the match is short-circuited, that person is returned as **302 Found**, and nothing is created.
- **The body supplies a `vanId` that matches nothing** — no error, and none of POST /people/create's blind echo: the id is ignored and the ordinary match runs on the rest of the payload — 302 when that matches, 201 UnmatchedStored when it does not.
- **One person record matches** — **302 Found**, with a `Location` header and `{"vanId": …, "status": "Matched"}`.
- **Several person records match** — still a **302** for exactly one of them, with nothing in the response to say the match was ambiguous. See POST /people/find for which one you get.
- **Nothing matches** — **201 Created** with `{"vanId": …, "status": "UnmatchedStored"}`, and the payload is stored as a new person record. Unlike find, this never returns 404 — the no-match case is the create case.
- **The criteria fall short of the minimum combination** — **201 Created** as well: a brand-new person record, even when the person is already in the database. This is the duplicate trap; see **The match half has a minimum threshold** below.
- **The body is empty (`{}`)** — every field is optional, including the name, so this is a no-match: **201** and a blank person record is created.

## The match half has a minimum threshold — below it, you create duplicates

The match runs under the same rules as POST /people/find: nothing is searched until the payload reaches one of these combinations:

- first name + last name + **email address**
- first name + last name + **phone**
- first name + last name + **zip5** + **date of birth**
- first name + last name + **street number + street name + zip5**
- **email address** on its own (a **phone** on its own works too)

**Below the threshold there is no "unmatched" to inspect — the API just creates a second person record.** Posting `{"firstName": "Harriet", "lastName": "Kowalski"}` for a person who is already in the database returns 201 with a fresh vanId, and the two person records now both exist. This is the main way duplicate person records get into a VAN database through the API.

So: only send a payload here that carries a strong identifier. If all you have is a name, search with GET /people first, decide for yourself whether a candidate is your person, and update it by id through POST /people/{vanId} instead.

## Differs from the official docs

- **the operation** — The docs present the minimum match combinations as a matching quality note; in practice, on this endpoint, falling short of them is what silently produces duplicate person records (observed 2026-08-04).

## Example

```bash
curl -sS -X POST \
  'https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/findOrCreate' \
  -u "app-name:$NGP_API_KEY|1" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
  "firstName": "Grace",
  "lastName": "Testperson",
  "emails": [
    {
      "email": "grace.testperson@example.com",
      "type": "W",
      "isPreferred": true
    }
  ]
}'
```

## Responses

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | Never sent by this endpoint. This is where a redirect-following client *lands* after a match: ``` POST /people/findOrCreate {"vanId": 102714558} ← 302 Found Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/102714558 {"vanId": 102714558, "status": "Matched"} GET /people/102714558 ← client re-issues the request at Location ← 200 OK { full person record — the body documented here } ``` So on a match your code sees this 200 and a full `Person`, not the 302 and its two-field match stub. `resp.history` (requests/httpx) or `resp.redirected` (fetch) is how you tell this apart from the 201 create path, which sends no `Location` and is never rewritten this way. See POST /people/find for the full redirect-following notes, including the `curl -X POST -L` gotcha. | [Person](../schemas/Person.md) |
| `201` | Nothing matched, so a new person record was created. No `Location` header is sent — the new id is in the body, and redirect-following clients see this response unchanged. | `PersonUnmatchedStored` |
| `302` | An existing person matched, so nothing was written. | `PersonMatched` |
| `400` | Validation error, as the standard JSON envelope. ([details](../ERRORS.md#badrequest)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) |
| `401` | Missing/invalid API key, or a database mode the key does not have access to. ([details](../ERRORS.md#unauthorized)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded. ([details](../ERRORS.md#toomanyrequests)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) |
| `500` | Internal server error. ([details](../ERRORS.md#servererror)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) or [AspNetError](../ERRORS.md#aspneterror) |

### `201` body — PersonUnmatchedStored

Nothing matched, so a new person record was created — the 201 body from findOrCreate.

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vanId` * | integer |  |
| `status` * | any |  |

`*` = required.

### `302` body — PersonMatched

An existing person was found and nothing was written. The only match-stub shape that accompanies a 302: from find, findOrCreate, create when the body's vanId exists, and update.

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vanId` * | integer |  |
| `status` * | any |  |

`*` = required.
